label: Rajput Painting
defn: Court painting of the Rajput kingdoms of Rajasthan and Central India, 16th–19th century, in schools named for their courts: Mewar Ragamala sets, Bundi and Kota hunting scenes, Kishangarh portraits of Radha, Jodhpur durbar paintings.

label: Pahari Painting
defn: Painting of the Hindu courts of the Punjab Hills, 17th–19th century, from the bold Basohli Rasamanjari to the lyrical Guler and Kangra Gita Govinda and Bhagavata Purana series of the family of Pandit Seu.

label: Jain Manuscript Painting
defn: The Western Indian style of manuscript painting on palm leaf and then paper (11th–16th century), chiefly Jain scriptures with angular figures and projecting far eyes: Kalpasutra, Kalakacharyakatha, painted wooden covers (patli).
aliases: Western Indian style;Jain painting;Western Indian painting

label: Sikh Painting
defn: Painting in the Punjab under Sikh patronage, late 18th–19th century, in Pahari and Company-influenced idioms: portraits of Ranjit Singh and his court, Janamsakhi illustrations, Gurus series.

label: Assamese Manuscript Painting
defn: Manuscript painting of Assam on sanchipat (agarwood-bark) folios, 16th–19th century, in sattriya and Ahom court styles: Hastividyarnava, illustrated Bhagavata.

label: Pattachitra
defn: Cloth-based painting of Odisha by the chitrakar community of Puri and Raghurajpur, in mineral colour on gum-and-chalk-primed cotton: Jagannath images, Gita Govinda panels, palm-leaf pothis.

label: Bengal Patachitra
defn: The narrative scroll painting of the patuas (chitrakars) of West Bengal and Bangladesh, unrolled frame by frame while the painter sings (pater gaan): Manasamangal scrolls, Jadupatua scrolls of the Santal.

label: Kalighat Painting
defn: Watercolours on mill paper sold by patua painters at the Kalighat temple in Calcutta, 19th–early 20th century, with bold outlines and satire of urban life: Durga and Kali icons, Tarakeswar scandal, babu and courtesan pictures.

label: Pichwai
defn: Large painted cloth hangings made at Nathdwara to hang behind the image of Shrinathji: Sharad Purnima, Annakut, cows and lotus ponds.

label: Mata ni Pachedi
defn: Ritual cloth shrines of the Vaghri community of Ahmedabad, hand-painted and block-printed in red and black around the Mother Goddess: Mata on her vahana, temple cloth panels.

label: Cheriyal Scroll Painting
defn: Narrative scrolls of Cheriyal in Telangana painted for the bardic storytellers of the Kaki Padagollu: Markandeya Purana scrolls, Gauda Purana.

label: Madhubani Painting
defn: The Mithila painting of women of Bihar and Nepal's Terai, moved from house walls to paper from the 1960s, in bharni, kachni and godna styles: kohbar ghar marriage paintings, Baua Devi nagas.

label: Warli Painting
defn: White rice-paste painting of the Warli of Maharashtra, from marriage chauk on house walls to works on paper (Jivya Soma Mashe): Palaghata chauk, tarpa dance circles.

label: Gond Painting
defn: The painting of the Pardhan Gond of Madhya Pradesh in dot-and-dash infill on paper and canvas since Jangarh Singh Shyam (Jangarh kalam): trees of life, Bhajju Shyam animals.

label: Tanjore Painting
defn: Devotional painting of Thanjavur on wooden board with gesso relief, gold leaf and glass stones, 18th–19th century: Balakrishna, Rama pattabhishekam.

label: Mysore Painting
defn: Devotional painting of the Mysore court in gesso and gold leaf, finer and lighter than Tanjore work: Krishna and Rama icons, Sritattvanidhi illustrations.

label: Truck Art
defn: The painted, mirrored and calligraphic decoration of lorries in Pakistan and India, from Rawalpindi, Peshawar and Karachi workshops: jingle trucks, Horn OK Please tailboards.
aliases: jingle truck;Truck art in South Asia

label: Rickshaw Painting
defn: Hand-painted cycle-rickshaw panels and hoods of Dhaka (UNESCO 2023), with film stars, landscapes and animals: backboard paintings, applique hoods.

label: Palm-Leaf Manuscripts
defn: Books of incised or inked palm leaves strung between wooden boards, the manuscript tradition of South Asia and Sri Lanka: Tamil and Grantha olas, Odia incised and painted pothis, Sinhalese Pali texts, Pala Buddhist Prajnaparamita.

label: Sanjhi
defn: Paper-stencil cutting of the Braj temples of Mathura and Vrindavan, used to lay coloured powder images: Krishna lila stencils.

label: Tholu Bommalata
defn: Shadow-puppet theatre of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka with large translucent painted-leather figures: Ramayana Ravana puppets, togalu gombeyata figures.

label: Gandharan Art
defn: Buddhist sculpture of Gandhara (Peshawar valley, Swat, Taxila), 1st century BCE–5th century CE, in schist and stucco with Hellenistic drapery: standing Buddhas, bodhisattva Maitreya, narrative stupa reliefs.

label: Art of Mathura
defn: The school of red-sandstone sculpture of Mathura (2nd century BCE–12th century), at its height under the Kushans and Guptas: Katra Buddha, yakshi railing pillars, Kanishka statue.

label: Amaravati Art
defn: The Andhra school of limestone relief sculpture of the Krishna valley under the Satavahanas and Ikshvakus: Amaravati stupa drum slabs, Nagarjunakonda friezes.

label: Pala Art
defn: The stone and bronze Buddhist and Hindu sculpture of Bengal and Bihar under the Palas and Senas (8th–12th century), in black basalt and eight-metal alloy: Kurkihar bronzes, Nalanda bodhisattvas, Surya steles.

label: Chola Bronzes
defn: Lost-wax bronze images cast in the Chola kingdom of Tamil Nadu (c. 850–1280) for temple processions: Shiva Nataraja, Somaskanda, Parvati.

label: Dhokra
defn: Lost-wax brass casting of tribal smiths of central and eastern India (Bastar, Bengal, Odisha) with wax-thread surfaces: Bastar horse and elephant figures, measure bowls.

label: Bankura Horse
defn: Stylised terracotta votive horses of Panchmura in Bankura, West Bengal, offered at village shrines.

label: Molela Terracotta
defn: Hand-modelled terracotta votive plaques of Molela in Rajasthan, made for shrines of Dharmaraja and Devnarayan.

label: Kaavad
defn: Portable painted wooden shrines of Bassi in Rajasthan whose hinged panels are opened by kaavadiya storytellers: Ram and Krishna kaavads.

label: Jaipur Blue Pottery
defn: Quartz-paste (fritware) vessels and tiles of Jaipur painted in cobalt and turquoise under a clear glaze, from the 19th century: surahis, tiles.

label: Banarasi Brocade
defn: Silk brocades woven with gold and silver zari in Varanasi, from Mughal kinkhab to the Banarasi sari: kinkhab, jangla and butidar saris.

label: Jamdani
defn: Supplementary-weft figured muslin of Dhaka and Bengal (UNESCO 2013), with motifs inlaid by hand on the loom: jamdani saris, Dhaka muslin.

label: Kanchipuram Silk
defn: Heavy mulberry-silk saris of Kanchipuram with contrast korvai borders and temple motifs.

label: Paithani
defn: Silk and zari saris of Paithan and Yeola in Maharashtra with tapestry-woven peacock and lotus pallus.

label: Phulkari
defn: Darn-stitch silk embroidery on khaddar of the women of Punjab, in sparse phulkari and fully covered bagh: bagh, chope.

label: Chikankari
defn: White-on-white shadow and knot-stitch embroidery of Lucknow on fine cotton.

label: Kantha
defn: Running-stitch embroidery on layered old cloth by the women of Bengal and Bangladesh: nakshi kantha, lep kantha.

label: Sujani
defn: Running-stitch embroidered quilts of Bhusura in Muzaffarpur, Bihar, with narrative figures.

label: Ralli Quilt
defn: Patchwork, applique and embroidered quilts of Sindh, Cholistan, Kutch and Rajasthan.

label: Indian Chintz
defn: Mordant-painted and resist-dyed cottons made on the Coromandel Coast and in Gujarat for export to Europe and Asia, 17th–18th century: palampores, Golconda floorspreads, petticoat panels for the Dutch market.

label: Kalamkari
defn: Pen-drawn and block-printed mordant-dyed cotton of Andhra Pradesh, in the Srikalahasti temple-cloth and Machilipatnam block-print styles: temple hangings, Persian-market prayer cloths.

label: Ajrakh
defn: Indigo and madder resist block-printed cotton of Sindh and Kutch, printed on both faces.

label: Bandhani
defn: Tie-dyed textiles of Gujarat and Rajasthan made by binding thousands of tiny points: gharchola, odhni.

label: Leheriya
defn: Diagonally tied and dyed wave-patterned turbans and saris of Rajasthan.

label: Patola
defn: Double-ikat silk saris of Patan in Gujarat, traded to Southeast Asia as heirloom cloths.

label: Rogan Art
defn: Cloth painted with a thickened castor-oil paste drawn from a stylus, practised at Nirona in Kutch.

label: Dumbara Mats
defn: Hana-fibre mats with symbolic motifs woven by the kinnara community of the Dumbara valley in Sri Lanka (UNESCO 2021).

label: Kondapalli Toys
defn: Carved and painted softwood (tella poniki) figures of Kondapalli in Andhra Pradesh: Dasavatara sets, ambari elephant.

label: Nirmal Toys
defn: Painted softwood toys and lacquered paintings of the Naqqash families of Nirmal in Telangana.

label: Channapatna Toys
defn: Lathe-turned wooden toys of Channapatna in Karnataka finished in coloured lac.

label: Etikoppaka Toys
defn: Lac-turned wooden toys of Etikoppaka in Andhra Pradesh coloured with vegetable dyes.

label: Bhimbetka Rock Paintings
defn: Painted rock shelters of the Vindhyan hills from the Mesolithic to the historical period (UNESCO 2003): hunting scenes, dancers, Zoo Rock.

label: Ajanta Paintings
defn: Buddhist cave murals of Ajanta (2nd century BCE–5th century CE), the classical model for Indian wall painting: Padmapani, Mahajanaka Jataka.

label: Sigiriya Frescoes
defn: The 5th-century paintings of women on the rock face of Kashyapa's palace at Sigiriya.

label: Kerala Mural Painting
defn: Temple and palace murals of Kerala (9th–19th century) in five colours: Mattancherry Palace Ramayana, Padmanabhapuram murals.

label: Kandyan Period Painting
defn: Buddhist temple murals of the Kandyan kingdom (1592–1815) in red and yellow narrative registers: Dambulla cave paintings, Degaldoruwa jatakas.

label: Shekhawati Frescoes
defn: Painted havelis, temples and forts of Shekhawati in Rajasthan, 18th–20th century, mixing Rajput, colonial and popular imagery.

label: Pithora Painting
defn: Ritual wall paintings of horses and deities by the Rathwa and Bhil of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.

label: Saura Painting
defn: Ritual wall paintings (ittal) of the Sora of Odisha dedicated to Idital.

label: Sohrai and Khovar Painting
defn: Harvest (sohrai) and marriage-chamber (khovar) wall paintings of Hazaribagh, Jharkhand.

label: Rangoli
defn: Ritual floor drawing in powder and rice paste across South Asia: kolam, alpana, kalamezhuthu.

label: Godna
defn: Tattooing of the tribal communities of central and eastern India (Baiga, Gond, Oraon), also transferred to painting on paper.

label: Mehndi
defn: Henna body painting of South Asia for weddings and festivals.

label: Thangka
defn: Buddhist painting on cotton or silk mounted in a textile frame to be hung, rolled and carried, the principal portable painting of Tibet, Bhutan, Ladakh and Mongolia: deity and lineage portraits, mandalas, wheel-of-life paintings, appliqué festival thangkas.
see: A4-8 Beri;A4-9 Menri;A4-10 Khyenri;A4-11 Karma Gadri;A4-13 Paubha;L2-13

label: Beri
defn: The Newar-derived style of Tibetan painting (13th–15th century) and its later continuations, with dense red and blue grounds and Nepalese figure canons: Sakya lineage thangkas, Ngor mandala sets.

label: Menri
defn: The central Tibetan painting tradition founded by Menla Döndrub (15th century), with Chinese-inspired landscape and a canon of peaceful deities, renewed as New Menri by Choying Gyatso at Tashi Lhunpo (17th century): arhat sets, lineage paintings.

label: Khyenri
defn: The central Tibetan painting style created by Khyentse Chenmo of Gongkar Chöde (15th century), known for wrathful deities, bright palettes and near-circular haloes: Gongkar Chöde murals, wrathful protector thangkas.

label: Karma Gadri
defn: The 'encampment' painting tradition of the Karma Kagyu, founded by Namkha Tashi (16th century) and renewed by Situ Panchen at Palpung (18th century), with open Chinese-style landscapes and pale grounds: Situ Panchen's Eight Great Mahasiddhas, Tenth Karmapa paintings.

label: Regong Arts
defn: The thangka painting (with murals, sculpture and appliqué) of the monastic artists of Rebkong (Tongren) in Amdo, from the 17th century to the present, on UNESCO's list since 2009: Wutun monastery thangkas, contemporary Rebkong painting.

label: Paubha
defn: Newar Buddhist and Hindu painting on cloth of the Kathmandu Valley, from the 12th century to the present, with flat red grounds and donor registers: Vasudhara mandalas, Chakrasamvara paubhas, long narrative vratha paintings.

label: Dunhuang Paintings
defn: The portable Buddhist paintings and banners on silk, hemp and paper deposited in the Library Cave (Cave 17) at the Mogao Caves, 8th–10th century: Tejaprabha and the Five Planets (897), bodhisattva banners, Famous Images of the Buddha.

label: Mongolian Calligraphy
defn: Writing as an art in the vertical Classical Mongolian script, with its six basic strokes, on paper, silk and wood (UNESCO 2013): sutra manuscripts, calligraphic scrolls.

label: Begram Ivories
defn: Carved ivory and bone plaques and furniture fittings of the 1st–2nd century found in the Kushan treasure at Begram (Kapisa) in Afghanistan, in an Indian idiom: river-goddess brackets, openwork throne-leg panels.

label: Nepalese Sculpture
defn: The metal, stone and wood sculpture of the Newars of the Kathmandu Valley from the Licchavi period on, above all gilt-copper images cast by lost wax and repoussé: standing Vajrapani (6th–7th c.), gilt-copper Taras, dancing Ganeshas.

label: Kashmiri Bronzes
defn: Buddhist and Hindu images cast in brass with silver and copper inlay in Kashmir (6th–12th century), largely preserved in Tibetan monasteries, the source of the Kashmiri (Kache) style of western Tibet: crowned Buddhas, Vajrasattva with silver-inlaid eyes.

label: Tibetan Buddhist Sculpture
defn: Images cast in gilt copper and brass, or modelled in clay and stucco, for Tibetan monasteries from the 11th century on, in Indian, Newar and Chinese-derived styles that fused into Tibetan workshops: Densatil stupa figures, portrait sculptures of lamas, Tsang gilt-copper images.

label: Zanabazar School
defn: The gilt-bronze sculpture of the first Jebtsundamba Khutukhtu Zanabazar (1635–1723) and his workshop at Tövkhön, in a Nepalese-derived style, and its Mongolian followers: White Tara, Vajradhara (1683), Five Dhyani Buddhas.

label: Sino-Tibetan Sculpture
defn: Tibetan Buddhist images made in Chinese imperial and northern workshops for Tibetan and Mongol patrons, from the Yuan atelier of Aniko through the Yongle and Xuande bronzes to Qing court and Dolonnor casting: Yongle-marked gilt bronzes, Kangxi gilt bronzes.

label: Sogdian Silver
defn: Chased, engraved and gilded silver vessels of the Sogdian city-states (6th–9th century), many found in the Urals and Siberia: cups with roundels of ibexes, bowls with banquet and hunting scenes.

label: Animal Style
defn: The art of the Eurasian steppe nomads (Scythian, Saka, Sarmatian, Ordos, Xiongnu), 9th century BCE–3rd century CE, in which stylised and contorted animals cover gold and bronze plaques, harness and weapons: curled-feline plaques, Arzhan deer, Ordos belt buckles.

label: Chakan
defn: The silk-on-cotton floral embroidery of Tajikistan for garments, coverlets and wall hangings (UNESCO 2018): chakan dresses, wall hangings.

label: Khamak
defn: The fine geometric satin-stitch embroidery of Kandahar and of Hazara women in Afghanistan, worked from the back on fine cotton: shirt panels, pillow covers, shawls.

label: Turkmen Needlework
defn: The embroidery applied to Turkmen dress of all ages and sexes in Turkmenistan and Iran, in chain, satin and stitch-band techniques (UNESCO 2022): chyrpy mantles, tahya caps.

label: Petroglyphs of the Mongolian Altai
defn: The rock carvings and paintings of the Mongolian Altai (UNESCO 2011), from about 11,000 years ago to the Turkic period: Tsagaan Salaa, Upper Tsagaan Gol, Aral Tolgoi.
aliases: Petroglyphic Complexes of the Mongolian Altai

label: Tamgaly Petroglyphs
defn: The Bronze Age to medieval rock carvings of Tamgaly and the Semirechye (UNESCO 2004), with sun-headed figures and sacrificial scenes: sun-headed deities, bull and chariot scenes.

label: Tibetan Buddhist Wall Paintings
defn: The secco murals of Tibetan Buddhist monasteries and temples across the Himalaya, from the Kashmiri-style programmes of Tabo and Alchi to Shalu, the Gyantse Kumbum and Guge: Alchi Sumtsek, Tabo assembly hall, Shalu murals.

label: Dunhuang Murals
defn: The wall paintings of the Buddhist cave temples of the Mogao Caves at Dunhuang (4th–14th century): Cave 217 Pure Land, Jataka narratives, donor portraits.

label: Kizil Murals
defn: The wall paintings of the Buddhist caves of the kingdom of Kucha (Kizil, Kumtura and neighbouring sites), 4th–8th century, in rhomboid narrative grids and lapis blue: Cave of the Sixteen Sword-Bearers, Buddha in Nirvana.

label: Bezeklik Murals
defn: The wall paintings of the Uyghur Buddhist caves of Bezeklik and the Turfan oasis (Qocho) under the Uyghur kingdom (9th–13th century): pranidhi scenes, Uyghur donor princes.
aliases: Bezeklik Thousand Buddha Caves murals;Uyghur Buddhist wall painting

label: Sogdian Wall Painting
defn: The secular and religious murals of Sogdian houses, temples and palaces (5th–8th century) at Panjikent, Afrasiyab and Varakhsha: Rustam cycle, Hall of the Ambassadors, Red Hall of Varakhsha.

label: Steppe Geoglyphs
defn: The earthen and stone ground figures of the Turgai Trough in northern Kazakhstan (Neolithic–Iron Age), at least 260 squares, rings and crosses: Ushtogay Square, Turgay triradial swastika.

label: Burmese Parabaik Painting
defn: Painting in watercolour on white parabaik (folding books of mulberry paper) by the royal and monastic painters of Konbaung Burma, 18th–19th century: court ceremonies and processions, Life of the Buddha, Jataka cycles, cosmologies.

label: Thai Manuscript Painting
defn: Paintings in gouache and gold on khoi-paper folding books of Siam, late 17th–19th century, chiefly funerary chanting books: Phra Malai manuscripts, Traiphum cosmologies, Ten Great Jatakas.
aliases: samut khoi painting;Phra Malai manuscript painting

label: Kamasan Painting
defn: The classical wayang-style painting of Kamasan village in Klungkung, Bali, on cloth and bark paper for temples and palaces since the Gelgel court (16th century): ider-ider friezes, langse hangings, palelintangan calendars, Kerta Gosa ceilings.
aliases: Kamasan wayang painting;wayang style painting;sangging Kamasan

label: Wayang Beber
defn: Javanese narrative scroll painting on dluwang bark paper, unrolled scene by scene by a dalang: Panji scrolls of Pacitan and Gunung Kidul.

label: Balinese Painting
defn: The modern painting of Bali from the late 1920s on paper and canvas, in the village schools that grew up around the Pita Maha association: Ubud genre and landscape, Batuan dense ink-and-wash scenes, Lempad's line drawings.

label: Sơn Mài
defn: Vietnamese lacquer painting on panel, developed as a fine art at the École des Beaux-Arts de l'Indochine from the 1930s: landscape and genre panels, gold- and eggshell-inlaid screens.

label: Letras y Figuras
defn: The 19th-century Philippine genre of watercolour letters composed of figures and scenes, with the costume pictures (tipos del país) of the same Manila painters: name monograms, Damián Domingo costume albums.

label: Đông Hồ Painting
defn: Woodblock prints of Đông Hồ village in Bắc Ninh on điệp (shell-coated) paper with natural colours, sold for Tết: Mouse Wedding, Jealousy, pig and piglets.

label: Hàng Trống Painting
defn: Hanoi's urban folk pictures, printed in outline from woodblocks and hand-coloured: Five Tigers, Carp Gazing at the Moon, Mother Goddess images.

label: Kim Hoàng Painting
defn: Woodblock prints of Kim Hoàng village west of Hanoi, printed on red or yellow paper: Tết pigs and roosters, calligraphic scrolls.

label: Lontar
defn: Manuscripts on incised leaves of the lontar palm, blackened with soot, the book form of Bali, Lombok and older Java: Kakawin Sutasoma, Nagarakretagama, illustrated prasi leaves.

label: Folding-Book Manuscripts
defn: Concertina-folded books of mulberry or khoi paper, lacquered at the ends, in Burma, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia: parabaik, samut khoi, Lanna phap sa, kraing.
aliases: folding book manuscript;parabaik;samut khoi;samut thai;kraing;phap sa

label: Kammavaca
defn: Burmese ordination texts written in square tamarind-seed script in lacquer and gold on lacquered palm leaf, cloth or metal: gilt kammavaca leaves, painted covers.

label: Pustaha
defn: The divination and ritual books of the Batak datu, written on folded tree bark between carved wooden covers: Great Pustaha.

label: Wayang Kulit
defn: The flat, pierced and painted buffalo-hide shadow puppets of Java and Bali (UNESCO 2003/2008), cut by named craftsmen: Arjuna and Bima figures, gunungan, Semar and the punakawan.

label: Wayang Golek
defn: Carved and painted wooden rod puppets of Sunda and Java, with the flat wooden wayang klitik of East Java: Sundanese Ramayana and Mahabharata sets, Menak cycle puppets.

label: Topeng
defn: Carved and painted wooden masks of Javanese and Balinese masked dance-drama: Panji masks of Cirebon and Malang, Balinese topeng pajegan sets.

label: Nang Yai
defn: Large perforated hide panels of the Thai court shadow theatre, each a whole scene from the Ramakien, with the small jointed puppets of southern nang talung: Wat Khanon panels.

label: Sbek Thom
defn: Large cut-hide panels of the Khmer shadow theatre (UNESCO 2005) performed with the Reamker.

label: Yoke Thé
defn: The carved, painted and costumed string marionettes of the Burmese court theatre: zawgyi alchemist, nat and princess figures.

label: Khmer Sculpture
defn: The stone and bronze sculpture of Cambodia and the Khmer lands from the pre-Angkor kingdoms to the Bayon (6th–13th century), in its successive temple styles: Harihara of Prasat Andet, Angkor Wat apsaras, Jayavarman VII portrait heads, Prakhon Chai bronzes.

label: Dvaravati Art
defn: The Buddhist sculpture of the Mon kingdoms of central Thailand (6th–11th century), in stone, bronze, terracotta and stucco: standing Buddhas with double vitarka, Dharmachakra wheels, Ku Bua terracottas.

label: Cham Sculpture
defn: The sandstone and bronze sculpture of the Cham kingdoms of central Vietnam (7th–15th century): Mỹ Sơn E1 pedestal, Đồng Dương Buddha and dvarapalas, Tháp Mẫm guardians.

label: Majapahit Terracotta
defn: Earthenware figurines, heads, reliefs and models from Trowulan and other East Javanese sites of the Majapahit era (13th–15th century): portrait heads, piggy banks, house models.

label: Bulul
defn: Carved wooden granary guardian figures of the Ifugao of northern Luzon, seated or standing, made in pairs.

label: Philippine Santos
defn: Carved and polychromed wooden and ivory devotional images made in the Spanish Philippines from the late 16th century, many for export to Mexico and Spain: Santo Niño, Virgin of the Immaculate Conception, ivory Christ child.

label: Dong Son Drums
defn: Bronze kettle drums of the Đông Sơn culture of northern Vietnam (c. 500 BCE–300 CE), cast with star-centred tympana, frogs and processions, traded across the archipelago: Ngọc Lũ drum, Hoàng Hạ drum, Makalamau of Sangeang.
aliases: Đông Sơn drums;Heger type I drums

label: Burmese Silver
defn: Repoussé and chased silver of Burma, 19th–early 20th century, with crowded narrative and zodiac friezes: offering bowls, betel boxes, presentation cups.

label: Kris
defn: The asymmetrical pattern-welded (pamor) dagger of Java and the Malay world (UNESCO 2005), with carved hilts and sheaths, in regional forms from Sumatra to Mindanao: Javanese keris with naga blade, Balinese figural hilts, Bugis sheaths, Moro kalis.

label: Javanese Gold Jewellery
defn: Gold ornaments of Hindu-Buddhist Java (8th–15th century), cast, repoussé and set with stones: sacred-thread clasps, ear ornaments, rings with Sri inscriptions, Wonoboyo hoard.

label: Ban Chiang Pottery
defn: Burial earthenware of the Ban Chiang culture of north-east Thailand, its late phase (c. 300 BCE–200 CE) painted with red swirls on buff: carinated jars with spirals, pedestal bowls.

label: Cham Pottery
defn: Hand-built, open-fired earthenware made by Cham women of Bình Thuận and Ninh Thuận (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2022): water jars, cooking pots.
aliases: Art of pottery-making of Chăm people;Bàu Trúc pottery

label: Kasongan Pottery
defn: Earthenware of Kasongan village near Yogyakarta, from votive animals to large decorated jars.

label: Khmer Ceramics
defn: The glazed stoneware of the Angkorian Khmer kilns of Cambodia and north-east Thailand (9th–14th century), in green and brown glazes: baluster jars, animal-form lime pots, roof finials.

label: Sawankhalok Ware
defn: Stoneware of the Si Satchanalai kilns in north-central Thailand (14th–16th century), celadon, brown and underglaze-black, exported widely to the archipelago: celadon dishes, covered boxes, figurines.

label: Vietnamese Ceramics
defn: Glazed stoneware of Vietnam from the Lý and Trần dynasties to the Lê export trade: Lý–Trần white and brown wares, Chu Đậu blue-and-white, Bát Tràng wares.

label: Bencharong
defn: Porcelain made in China to Thai order and enamelled in five colours on a black or coloured ground for the Ayutthaya and Bangkok courts: covered bowls, thepanom-figure jars.

label: Songket
defn: Silk or cotton brocade with supplementary weft of gold and silver thread, woven in the Malay courts of Sumatra, the Peninsula and Brunei: Palembang songket, Minangkabau songket.

label: Lampung Ship Cloths
defn: Supplementary-weft ceremonial cloths of the Lampung of south Sumatra depicting ships of the soul: the large aristocratic palepai banners and the ubiquitous tampan.

label: Piña
defn: Sheer cloth woven from pineapple-leaf fibre in Aklan and Manila, often embroidered (calado), made into barong and pañuelo.

label: Inabel
defn: The cotton handloom weaving of the Ilocos region of Luzon, in binakol whirlpool and other patterns.

label: Naga Motif Weaving in Lao Communities
defn: Handwoven Lao silks with naga serpent motifs in supplementary weft and ikat (UNESCO 2023): sinh skirts, pha biang shoulder cloths.

label: Tapis
defn: The ceremonial tube skirts of Lampung women, warp-ikat and woven grounds couched with gold thread, mica and embroidery.

label: Kalaga
defn: Burmese padded appliqué hangings embroidered with sequins and metal thread in scenes from the Jatakas and court life.

label: Tekat
defn: Malay raised gold-thread embroidery couched over card or padding, for cushions, betel covers and wedding furnishings.

label: Indonesian Batik
defn: Wax-resist dyed cloth of Java (UNESCO 2009), drawn by canting (tulis) or stamped (cap), in the court styles of Yogyakarta and Surakarta and the coastal pesisir styles of Pekalongan, Lasem and Cirebon: parang rusak kain, batik Belanda, Hokokai batik.

label: Malaysian Batik
defn: Block-printed and hand-drawn batik of the east-coast Malay states, Kelantan and Terengganu, with large floral designs.

label: Indonesian Ikat
defn: Warp-ikat cotton cloths of the eastern islands and of Sumatra, Borneo and Sulawesi, tied and dyed in morinda and indigo: Sumba hinggi mantles, Toraja sacred cloths, Savu and Flores sarongs.

label: Geringsing
defn: The double-ikat cotton cloths of Tenganan Pegeringsingan in Bali, worn for protection in rites.

label: Tais
defn: Handwoven textiles of Timor-Leste (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2021), in ikat, supplementary weft and tapestry.

label: Pua Kumbu
defn: The ceremonial warp-ikat blankets of the Iban of Sarawak and Kalimantan, woven by women with spirit and ancestor figures.

label: T'nalak
defn: Abaca warp-ikat cloth of the T'boli of South Cotabato, its designs dreamed by the weaver.

label: Telepuk
defn: Malay cloth stamped with gold leaf from carved wooden blocks for court and wedding dress.

label: Noken
defn: Knotted and woven string bags of bark fibre and orchid stem made by women of Papua (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2012).

label: Daluang
defn: Javanese beaten-bark paper (dluwang) of paper mulberry, made in Ponorogo and Garut and used for pesantren and wayang beber manuscripts.

label: Malay Woodcarving
defn: The carved wood of the Malay Peninsula, above all of Kelantan and Terengganu, for palaces, houses, boats and weapon hilts, in pierced floral (awan larat) designs.

label: Burmese Lacquerware
defn: Coiled-bamboo and horsehair vessels coated in thitsi lacquer, engraved (yun) or gilded and glass-inlaid, made above all in Bagan: offering vessels (hsun-ok), betel boxes, manuscript chests.

label: Lai Rot Nam
defn: Thai gold-and-black lacquer decoration on wood, made by gold leaf on a lacquer ground with a water-washed resist: manuscript cabinets, temple doors and window shutters.

label: Maros-Pangkep Cave Art
defn: Painted and stencilled rock art of the limestone karst of South Sulawesi, among the oldest figurative art known (45,000+ years): Leang Tedongnge warty pig, Leang Bulu' Sipong 4 hunting scene, hand stencils.

label: Sangkulirang-Mangkalihat Rock Art
defn: Hand stencils and animal paintings of the limestone caves of East Kalimantan and of Niah in Sarawak: Lubang Jeriji Saléh banteng, Niah Painted Cave.

label: Bagan Murals
defn: The tempera wall paintings of the temples of Bagan (11th–13th century) and their Inwa and Konbaung successors: Abeyadana, Lokahteikpan Jatakas, Ananda temple.

label: Thai Mural Painting
defn: Tempera wall paintings of Thai Buddhist ordination halls and viharas, late Ayutthaya to early Rattanakosin and Lanna: Wat Phra Kaew Ramakien, Wat Pho, Wat Phumin, Wat Chong Nonsi.

label: Sak Yant
defn: Thai, Khmer, Lao and Burmese protective yantra tattooing of sacred diagrams and Khom script, applied by monks and ajarn with a steel rod.

label: Mentawai Tattooing
defn: The full-body line tattooing (titi) of the Mentawai of Siberut, west of Sumatra.

label: Batok
defn: The traditional tattooing of the Philippines, from the Visayan pintados to the Kalinga and Bontoc warrior tattoos.

label: Ethiopian Manuscript Painting
defn: Painting in Ethiopian Christian manuscripts on parchment, from the Aksumite-era gospel books to the Gondarine Marian miracle books: Garima Gospels evangelist portraits, Miracles of Mary (Täammərä Maryam) cycles, illustrated Psalters.

label: Ethiopian Manuscripts
defn: The Ge'ez (and later Amharic) manuscript tradition of the Ethiopian and Eritrean church: parchment codices in wooden boards with blind-tooled leather, written in Ge'ez script with ornamental harag frames: gospel books, Psalters, Arganonä Maryam prayer books.

label: Ethiopian Icon Painting
defn: Panel painting of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church from the 15th century, in tempera on gessoed wood (later over glued cloth), as diptychs, triptychs and processional icons, in the styles named First and Second Gondarine: Virgin and Child with archangels, St George on horseback, Kwer'ata Re'esu.

label: Ethiopian Magic Scrolls
defn: Protective parchment scrolls cut to the owner's height and painted by däbtära (church-trained scholars) with talismanic figures, eyes, angels and nets beside Ge'ez prayers: healing scrolls, talismanic eyes and faces, Solomon's net designs.

label: Tingatinga Painting
defn: The Dar es Salaam school of enamel painting on board founded by Edward Said Tingatinga in 1968 and carried on by his followers and the Tingatinga Arts Cooperative: flat-coloured animals and birds, crowded village and spirit scenes.

label: Benin Ivories
defn: Ivory carved for the Oba of Benin by the Igbesanmwan guild and in neighbouring Owo, 15th–19th century: pendant masks of the Iyoba Idia, carved tusks for royal altars, double gongs and armlets.
attest: wiki:Art of the Kingdom of Benin

label: Afro-Portuguese Ivories
defn: Ivories carved by Sapi (Sierra Leone), Edo (Benin) and Kongo carvers for Portuguese patrons in the 15th–16th century: salt cellars, side-blown oliphants, spoons and pyxes.

label: Dogon Masks
defn: Masks of the Dogon Awa society danced at the dama funerary rites and the Sigi, carved in wood with rectangular faces and superstructures: kanaga, satimbe, sirige (storeyed house), imina na (great mask).

label: Chiwara
defn: Antelope crest headdresses of the Bamana Ciwara association, danced in pairs at planting and harvest, in vertical, horizontal and abstract regional styles: male and female pairs, vertical Bamako-region crests, horizontal Ségou crests.

label: Senufo Masks
defn: Masks and helmet masks of the Senufo Poro and Tyekpa societies of northern Côte d'Ivoire, Mali and Burkina Faso: kpeliye'e face masks, kponyugu fire-spitter helmet masks, wanyugo helmets.

label: Chokwe Masks
defn: Masks of the Chokwe of Angola, Zambia and the DR Congo danced at mukanda initiation and festivals: mwana pwo (young woman) masks, cihongo male masks, resin-and-barkcloth initiation masks.

label: Gelede
defn: Masks of the Yoruba (Ketu, Egbado, Anago) Gelede society, danced in pairs to honour the mothers: helmet masks with carved superstructures, Efe night masks.

label: Igbo Masks
defn: Masks and masquerades of the Igbo of south-eastern Nigeria, by village and society: agbogho mmuo maiden-spirit masks, Ijele towering masquerade, Afikpo okumkpa masks, Izzi elephant-spirit helmets.

label: Dan Masks
defn: Wooden face masks of the Dan (Gio, Yacouba) of Liberia and Côte d'Ivoire, with polished oval faces, slit or round eyes and named spirit roles: deangle masks, gunyege racing masks, ma go miniature masks.

label: Sowei Masks
defn: Black helmet masks of the women's Sande society of the Mende, Vai, Temne and Gola of Sierra Leone and Liberia, with neck rings and elaborate coiffures: ndoli jowei, sowo gande masterworks.

label: Kuba Masks
defn: The royal masks of the Kuba kingdom, danced as a trio of founding figures: mwaash aMbooy, ngady amwaash, bwoom.

label: Kifwebe
defn: Striated masks of the Songye and Luba bwadi bwa kifwebe society: male crested kifwebe, female white kifwebe.

label: Pende Masks
defn: Masks of the Central and Kwilu Pende of the DR Congo, danced at mbuya village masquerades and chiefs' rites, with their ivory miniatures: mbuya character masks, giwoyo and kipoko masks, ikhoko pendants.

label: Punu Masks
defn: The white-faced okuyi masks of the Punu and Lumbo of southern Gabon, danced on stilts: okuyi maiden masks.

label: Nok Terracottas
defn: Terracotta sculpture of the Nok culture of central Nigeria (c. 900 BCE–300 CE), hollow-built figures and heads with triangular pierced eyes and elaborate coiffures; the related Sokoto and Katsina Ala styles are kinds: seated figures, heads, animal figures.

label: Ife Art
defn: The classical sculpture of Ile-Ife (c. 1000–1450) in copper alloy and terracotta: naturalistic heads and figures of rulers and court: Wunmonije heads, Obalufon mask, terracotta heads from shrine sites.

label: Benin Bronzes
defn: Cast brass of the Edo court of Benin, 13th–19th century, by the Igun Eronmwon guild: palace plaques, commemorative heads for royal altars, figures of the Iyoba and of Portuguese, altarpieces.
see: Benin Ivories;Ife Art;Lower Niger Bronze Industry

label: Lower Niger Bronze Industry
defn: Fagg's name for copper-alloy castings of the 14th–16th centuries from the lower Niger that fit neither Ife nor Benin, among them the Tsoede bronzes of Tada and Jebba: Tada seated figure, Jebba bowman, bells and plaques.

label: Esie Soapstone Figures
defn: Over a thousand soapstone figures of seated men and women (c. 12th–15th century) found at Esie in Yoruba-speaking Kwara State, the largest corpus of stone sculpture in sub-Saharan Africa.

label: Djenné Terracottas
defn: Terracotta sculpture of the Inland Niger Delta (c. 1100–1600), from Djenné-Djeno and neighbouring sites: kneeling and seated figures, figures covered with pustules or snakes, equestrian figures; Bankoni is a related style.
aliases: Inland Niger Delta terracottas;Jenne terracottas;Middle Niger terracottas

label: Bura Terracottas
defn: Funerary terracottas of the Bura culture of Niger and Burkina Faso (c. 200–1100): cylindrical heads on jar burials, equestrian figures.

label: Koma Terracottas
defn: Terracotta figures and heads from burial mounds of Komaland in northern Ghana (c. 1100–1700), many heavily looted: stylised heads, equestrian figures.

label: Sao Terracottas
defn: Terracotta and copper-alloy sculpture of the Sao civilisation south of Lake Chad (c. 500–1600): human and animal heads, funerary jars.

label: Lydenburg Heads
defn: Seven hollow terracotta heads of the Early Iron Age (c. 500 CE) from Lydenburg in Mpumalanga, the earliest known sculpture of southern Africa.

label: Nomoli
defn: Small stone figures (soapstone, steatite) of the Sapi peoples of Sierra Leone and Guinea (c. 1400–1600), found in fields by later Mende and Kissi farmers: seated nomoli, larger pomdo heads.

label: Zimbabwe Birds
defn: The eight soapstone birds on columns from Great Zimbabwe (c. 13th–15th century).

label: Yoruba Sculpture
defn: Wood sculpture of the Yoruba of Nigeria and Benin, carved by named masters and workshops for shrines, palaces and divination: ere ibeji twin figures, Ifa divination trays and bowls, Ogboni edan brass pairs, veranda posts by Olowe of Ise.

label: Dogon Sculpture
defn: Wood sculpture of the Dogon of the Bandiagara escarpment, Mali, with the earlier Tellem figures: primordial couples, figures with raised arms, granary doors and locks, hogon cups.

label: Bamana Sculpture
defn: Wood and iron sculpture of the Bamana (Bambara) of Mali, carved by numu blacksmiths: jonyeleni and gwan maternity figures, boli power objects, n'tomo and kore masks.

label: Senufo Sculpture
defn: Wood sculpture of the Senufo of Côte d'Ivoire, Mali and Burkina Faso by carver groups (kulebele, fonombele): pombia (child of Poro) figures, deble rhythm pounders, madeo divination figures, kalao hornbills.

label: Baule Sculpture
defn: Wood sculpture of the Baule of Côte d'Ivoire, polished and finely detailed: blolo bla and blolo bian spirit-spouse figures, asie usu nature-spirit figures, goli and mblo masks, heddle pulleys.

label: Lobi Sculpture
defn: Wood figures of the Lobi of Burkina Faso, Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire made for thil shrines: bateba figures in gesture, heads on posts.

label: Akan Sculpture
defn: Wood and terracotta sculpture of the Akan (Asante, Fante, Anyi) of Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire: akuaba fertility figures, mma terracotta memorial heads, linguist staff finials, stools.

label: Chokwe Sculpture
defn: Court sculpture of the Chokwe of Angola and the DR Congo, 19th century: Chibinda Ilunga hunter-hero figures, mwanangana chiefs' figures, royal chairs and stools.

label: Luba Sculpture
defn: Court sculpture of the Luba of the south-eastern DR Congo: caryatid stools, bowl bearers, headrests, lukasa memory boards, staffs of office.

label: Lega Sculpture
defn: Ivory, bone and wood figures and masks owned by grades of the Lega bwami association, eastern DR Congo: iginga figurines, lukwakongo masks.

label: Ndop
defn: Commemorative portrait figures of the Kuba kings (nyim), each carved with his emblem (ibol), 18th–19th century.

label: Makonde Sculpture
defn: Carving of the Makonde of Tanzania and Mozambique: lipiko helmet masks and figures, and from the 1950s the ebony sculpture of Dar es Salaam: mapiko masks, shetani figures, ujamaa trees of life.

label: Fantasy Coffins
defn: Figurative coffins carved by Ga carpenters in Teshie and Nungua near Accra since the 1950s, shaped after the deceased's trade or emblem: fish, cocoa-pod and car coffins.

label: Minkisi
defn: Power objects of the Kongo peoples, figures and containers charged with medicines by a nganga; Songye and Teke power figures are kinds: nkondi nail figures, nkisi in animal form, Songye mankishi.

label: Fang Reliquary Guardians
defn: Wooden figures and heads set on bark boxes of ancestral relics by the Fang of Gabon, Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea: eyema byeri figures, byeri heads.

label: Asen
defn: Iron and brass memorial altars of the Fon of Benin (Abomey, Ouidah): a staff topped by a cone with cut-out figures and emblems commemorating the dead.

label: Ethiopian Crosses
defn: Processional, hand and pectoral crosses of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church in cast brass, silver and carved wood, with openwork lattices: Lalibela processional crosses, Gondar crosses, hand crosses.

label: Akan Goldweights
defn: Small brass weights cast by lost wax by the Akan for weighing gold dust, geometric and figurative (proverbs): abrammuo, with kuduo vessels and forowa boxes of the same casters.

label: Igbo-Ukwu Bronzes
defn: Leaded-bronze vessels and regalia cast by lost wax at Igbo-Ukwu (9th–10th century), with dense granular surfaces: roped pot, shell-shaped bowl, pendant ornaments.

label: Kente Cloth
defn: Strip-woven silk and cotton cloth of the Asante and Ewe of Ghana and Togo, narrow strips with named warp and weft-float patterns sewn edge to edge: adwini asa, oyokoman, Ewe kente.

label: Aso Oke
defn: Prestige strip-woven cloth of the Yoruba of Nigeria: sanyan, alaari, etu.

label: Akwete Cloth
defn: Cloth woven by Ndoki Igbo women of Akwete on the vertical loom, with the ikaki (tortoise) motif.

label: Ivorian Loincloth Weaving
defn: The traditional loincloth (pagne) weaving of Côte d'Ivoire, strip-woven on narrow looms (Baule, Senufo, Dioula, Dan), inscribed by UNESCO in 2023.

label: Kuba Raffia Textiles
defn: Raffia cloth of the Kuba peoples of the DR Congo, woven by men and embroidered by women: Shoowa cut-pile ('Kasai velvet') panels, appliqué overskirts, Bushoong ceremonial skirts.

label: Asafo Flags
defn: Appliqué regimental flags (frankaa) of the Fante Asafo companies of coastal Ghana, with proverb designs and a corner Union Jack or Ghanaian flag.

label: Bògòlanfini
defn: Mud-dyed cotton cloth of the Bamana of Mali, strip-woven by men and painted by women with fermented mud on a leaf-dye ground.

label: Adire
defn: Indigo resist-dyed cloth of Yoruba women: adire eleko (starch resist), adire oniko (tied), adire alabere (stitched).

label: Adinkra Cloth
defn: Asante funerary and prestige cloth stamped with calabash stamps of named adinkra symbols, centred on Ntonso.

label: Ndop Cloth
defn: Indigo stitch-resist royal display cloth of the Cameroon Grassfields (Bamileke, Bamum), strip-woven and patterned in white.

label: Kanga
defn: Printed cotton cloths of the Swahili coast worn in pairs, with a border, central field and a printed Swahili proverb (jina): kanga, kitenge.

label: Ugandan Barkcloth
defn: Barkcloth beaten from the inner bark of the mutuba fig by Baganda craftsmen, terracotta-coloured, for royal and funerary use (UNESCO 2008).

label: Mbuti Barkcloth
defn: Barkcloth of the Mbuti of the Ituri forest, prepared by men and painted by women with linear and dotted designs in gardenia and charcoal.

label: Agaseke
defn: Coiled lidded baskets of Rwanda with conical lids and geometric patterns, made by women.

label: Zulu Beadwork
defn: Glass-bead regalia of the Zulu of KwaZulu-Natal in brick stitch, with colour codes by region and age: ucu necklaces, love-letter panels (incwadi), beaded aprons and skirts.

label: Maasai Beadwork
defn: Beaded collars, earrings and headdresses of the Maasai of Kenya and Tanzania: flat disc collars, wedding necklaces.

label: Yoruba Beadwork
defn: Beaded regalia of Yoruba kings and Ifa priests: beaded crowns with veils (ade), diviners' bags, beaded staffs.

label: Kgatleng Pottery
defn: Earthenware pottery made by Bakgatla women potters in the Kgatleng District of Botswana, burnished and decorated (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2012).

label: Saharan Rock Art
defn: Engraved and painted rock art of the Sahara from the Holocene to historical times, by stylistic phases: Bubaline engravings, Round Head paintings, Bovidian (pastoral) paintings, Dabous giraffes.

label: San Rock Art
defn: Painted and engraved rock art of the San (Bushmen) of southern Africa, over tens of thousands of years: Drakensberg eland paintings, Twyfelfontein engravings, Tsodilo paintings.

label: Ethiopian Church Painting
defn: Wall painting of Ethiopian churches, on plaster and on canvas glued to walls: Debre Berhan Selassie ceiling of winged faces, Lake Tana monastery murals, Lalibela paintings.

label: Litema
defn: Incised and painted mud-wall decoration of Basotho homesteads in Lesotho and the Free State, renewed by women.

label: Ndebele House Painting
defn: Geometric mural painting of the Southern Ndebele of South Africa on homestead walls, by women (Esther Mahlangu).

label: Imigongo
defn: Rwandan relief panels of cow dung in black, white and red spirals and zigzags, from house walls to boards.

label: African Scarification
defn: Cicatrisation and keloid scarification as body art across Africa, with named regional marks: Yoruba facial marks (ila), Nuba and Dinka marks.

label: Sona
defn: Sand drawings (lusona, pl. sona) of the Chokwe and neighbouring peoples of eastern Angola: continuous lines around a grid of dots, illustrating stories.

label: Byzantine Illuminated Manuscripts
defn: Painted miniatures in Greek manuscripts of the Byzantine empire, 4th–15th century, from late antique codices to the classicising Macedonian Renaissance and Palaiologan books: Vienna Dioscurides, Rossano Gospels, Paris Psalter, Menologion of Basil II.

label: Byzantine Icons
defn: Devotional images painted in encaustic or egg tempera on wooden panels in the Byzantine empire and its orbit, 6th–15th century: Sinai Christ Pantokrator, Theotokos of Vladimir, Hodegetria and Deesis icons.

label: Cretan School
defn: Post-Byzantine icon painting of Venetian Crete, 15th–17th century, joining the Palaiologan manner with Italian elements: icons of Andreas Ritzos and Michael Damaskinos, Theophanes the Cretan's Athonite murals.

label: Fayum Mummy Portraits
defn: Portraits painted in encaustic or tempera on wooden panels and bound over the faces of mummies in Roman Egypt, 1st–3rd century: Hawara and Er-Rubayat portraits, Tomb of Aline, portraits from Antinoöpolis.

label: Book of the Dead
defn: Illustrated Egyptian funerary papyri of spells for the afterlife, with painted vignettes, New Kingdom to Ptolemaic: Papyrus of Ani, Papyrus of Hunefer, Greenfield Papyrus.
aliases: Egyptian funerary papyri;Coming Forth by Day

label: Assyrian Palace Reliefs
defn: Carved gypsum orthostat reliefs from Neo-Assyrian palaces, 9th–7th century BC, with lamassu gateway figures: Ashurnasirpal II at Nimrud, Sennacherib's Lachish reliefs, Ashurbanipal's lion hunt.

label: Nimrud Ivories
defn: Carved, gilded and inlaid ivory plaques and figures of the 9th–7th century BC found at the Assyrian capital Nimrud, made in Assyrian, Phoenician and North Syrian styles: Lioness attacking a Nubian, Woman at the Window, furniture plaques.

label: Byzantine Ivories
defn: Ivory carving of the Byzantine empire, 5th–12th century: consular diptychs, Barberini Ivory, Romanos group icons, Veroli Casket.

label: Cylinder Seals
defn: Engraved stone cylinders rolled on clay to leave a continuous image, the glyptic art of Mesopotamia, Iran, Syria and Anatolia from the Uruk period to the Achaemenids: Uruk and Jemdet Nasr seals, Akkadian contest scenes, Old Syrian and Mitanni seals, Neo-Assyrian ritual scenes.

label: Minoan Seals
defn: Engraved sealstones of hardstone, bone and gold made on Bronze Age Crete and adopted on the Mycenaean mainland, 3rd–2nd millennium BC: lentoid and amygdaloid seals, Pylos Combat Agate, gold signet rings.

label: Engraved Gems
defn: Intaglios and cameos cut in hardstone in the Greek, Etruscan and Roman world, 6th century BC – 4th century AD: Graeco-Persian gems, Etruscan scarabs, Roman Republican ringstones, Gemma Augustea.

label: Ancient Egyptian Sculpture
defn: Statuary and relief of pharaonic Egypt in stone, wood and metal, from the Old Kingdom to the Ptolemies: Menkaure triad, Middle Kingdom block statues and tomb models, Amarna reliefs, sunk temple relief.

label: Cycladic Figures
defn: Marble figures, mostly folded-arm female figures, made in the Cyclades in the Early Bronze Age, 3rd millennium BC: Spedos and Dokathismata types, harp player from Keros, marble vessels.

label: Ancient Greek Sculpture
defn: Stone and bronze sculpture of the Greek world from the Archaic to the Hellenistic period: kouroi and korai, Parthenon marbles, Riace bronzes, Pergamon Altar.

label: Greek Terracotta Figurines
defn: Mould-made and painted clay figurines of the Greek world, votive and decorative, Archaic to Hellenistic: Tanagra figurines, Tarentine votive figures, Myrina figurines, Boeotian figures.

label: Etruscan Sculpture
defn: Sculpture of Etruria in terracotta, bronze, stone and alabaster, 7th–1st century BC: Sarcophagus of the Spouses, Apollo of Veii, Chimera of Arezzo, Volterran cinerary urns.

label: Roman Portraiture
defn: Portrait sculpture of ancient Rome in marble and bronze, from veristic Republican heads to imperial portraits: Patrician Torlonia, Augustus of Prima Porta, Severan and Tetrarchic portraits.

label: Roman Sculpture
defn: Roman sculpture other than portraits: historical relief, ideal statuary and copies after Greek works, and carved sarcophagi: Ara Pacis, Trajan's Column, Ludovisi sarcophagus.

label: Luristan Bronzes
defn: Cast bronze horse-bits, finials, standards, pins and weapons from the Zagros mountains of western Iran, early 1st millennium BC: master-of-animals finials, cheekpieces with winged creatures, votive pins.

label: Achaemenid Metalwork
defn: Gold and silver vessels and ornaments of the Persian empire, 6th–4th century BC: gold fluted bowls and rhyta, Oxus Treasure, griffin-handled amphorae.

label: Sasanian Silver
defn: Silver and silver-gilt vessels of Sasanian Iran, 3rd–7th century, hammered and chased with royal hunts and Dionysiac scenes: royal hunting plates, ewers with dancing figures, high-footed bowls.

label: Etruscan Mirrors
defn: Bronze hand mirrors of Etruria and Latium with mythological scenes engraved on the back, 6th–2nd century BC, together with the engraved cistae of Praeneste: mirror with Minerva and Hercules, Ficoroni Cista.

label: Geometric Pottery
defn: Greek painted pottery of c. 900–700 BC with banded meanders and, in its late phase, figural funeral and battle scenes: Dipylon amphora, Hirschfeld Krater, Protogeometric amphorae.

label: Corinthian Vase Painting
defn: Painted pottery of Corinth, 725–550 BC, where black-figure was invented: miniature Protocorinthian aryballoi such as the Chigi olpe, and Corinthian animal-frieze kraters and alabastra.

label: Black-Figure Pottery
defn: Greek vase painting with figures painted in black slip and incised on the red clay, above all in Attica, c. 620–480 BC: François Vase, Exekias's Achilles and Ajax amphora, Panathenaic prize amphorae.

label: Red-Figure Pottery
defn: Greek vase painting with figures reserved in the red clay on a black ground, invented in Athens c. 530 BC and carried to South Italy: Euphronios Krater, Berlin Painter's amphorae, Niobid Krater.

label: Laconian Vase Painting
defn: Black-figure and earlier painted pottery of Sparta and Laconia, 7th–6th century BC: Arkesilas Cup, cups of the Hunt and Naucratis Painters.

label: East Greek Vase Painting
defn: Painted pottery of the Ionian coast and East Aegean islands, 7th–6th century BC: Wild Goat Style oinochoai, Fikellura amphorae, Klazomenian sarcophagi and vases, Chian chalices.

label: South Italian Vase Painting
defn: Red-figure pottery made by Greek workshops of Magna Graecia and Sicily, late 5th–3rd century BC, in its Apulian, Lucanian, Campanian, Paestan and Sicilian fabrics: Darius Vase, Asteas's phlyax kraters.
aliases: South Italian ancient Greek pottery;Italiote vase painting

label: Gnathia Vases
defn: Black-glazed pottery of Apulia painted over the glaze in white, yellow and red, c. 370–250 BC: Gnathia skyphoi and oinochoai with vines, masks and garlands.

label: Centuripe Ware
defn: Hellenistic Sicilian pottery painted in tempera after firing, with pink grounds and figures in relief, 3rd–2nd century BC: lebetes and lekanides from Centuripe and Morgantina.

label: Etruscan Vase Painting
defn: Painted pottery of Etruria, 7th–3rd century BC, from Etrusco-Corinthian and black-figure to red-figure workshops at Vulci and Falerii: Pontic Group amphorae, Caeretan hydriae, Genucilia plates.

label: Bucchero
defn: The black, burnished, reduction-fired pottery of the Etruscans, 7th–5th century BC, from thin-walled bucchero sottile to moulded heavy bucchero: kantharoi, stamped oinochoai, rhyta.

label: Minoan Pottery
defn: Painted pottery of Bronze Age Crete, from Vasiliki ware through polychrome Kamares ware to the Marine and Floral Styles: Kamares cups, Octopus flask from Palaikastro, Palace Style jars.

label: Mycenaean Pottery
defn: Painted pottery of Late Bronze Age mainland Greece, c. 1600–1100 BC, traded across the Mediterranean: stirrup jars, pictorial chariot kraters, Warrior Vase.

label: Terra Sigillata
defn: The glossy red-slipped Roman tableware, plain and mould-decorated, made in Arezzo, Gaul, Germany and North Africa, 1st century BC – 3rd century AD: Arretine ware, South Gaulish samian bowls, African red slip ware.

label: Hadra Vases
defn: Hellenistic cinerary hydriae painted on a light slip, used for burials at the Hadra cemetery of Alexandria, 3rd century BC: Laurel Group and Dolphin Group hydriae.

label: Kerma Ware
defn: The thin, polished, black-topped red pottery of the Kerma kingdom of Upper Nubia, c. 2500–1500 BC: Classic Kerma bell-shaped beakers with a grey band.

label: Meroitic Pottery
defn: Wheel-made fine ware of the Meroitic kingdom of Kush, 1st century BC – 4th century AD, painted with religious emblems, plants and animals: painted jars and cups from Karanog and Faras.

label: Nabataean Pottery
defn: The eggshell-thin painted fine ware of the Nabataeans of Petra, 1st century BC – 2nd century AD, decorated with leaves and palmettes: Nabataean painted bowls.

label: Egyptian Faience
defn: Glazed sintered-quartz ware of ancient Egypt, blue and green, used for small sculpture, amulets, vessels and inlay: scarabs, ushabti figures, blue hippopotamus figurines, lotus chalices.

label: Roman Glass
defn: Blown, mould-blown, cast and cut glass of the Roman empire, 1st century BC – 5th century AD, made in Syria, Italy, Egypt and the Rhineland: Ennion's mould-blown cups, Portland Vase, Lycurgus cage cup.

label: Hellenistic Glass
defn: Core-formed, cast and mosaic glass of the Greek world and the Eastern Mediterranean, 6th–1st century BC: core-formed alabastra and amphoriskoi, cast bowls, gold-sandwich glass.

label: Coptic Textiles
defn: Tapestry-woven linen and wool textiles of late antique and early Islamic Egypt, 3rd–8th century, from burial grounds: tunic clavi and roundels, hangings with Dionysiac and Nilotic scenes, weft-loop wall hangings.

label: Sasanian Rock Reliefs
defn: Royal reliefs carved on cliff faces in Fars and western Iran by the Sasanian kings, 3rd–7th century, following Achaemenid precedent: Naqsh-e Rostam investitures, Bishapur triumph of Shapur I, Taq-e Bostan.

label: Hittite Rock Reliefs
defn: Reliefs of gods and kings carved on rock in Hittite Anatolia, 14th–13th century BC: Yazılıkaya, Fraktin, Hanyeri, Taşçı.

label: Gobustan Rock Art
defn: Petroglyphs of hunters, dancers, animals and reed boats pecked into the rocks of Gobustan in Azerbaijan from the late Upper Palaeolithic onward (UNESCO 2007).

label: Rock Art in the Hail Region
defn: Petroglyphs of humans, animals and inscriptions at Jubbah and Shuwaymis in the Ha'il region of Saudi Arabia, spanning some 10,000 years (UNESCO 2015).
aliases: Hail rock art;Jubbah and Shuwaymis petroglyphs

label: Egyptian Tomb Painting
defn: Wall painting in the tombs and temples of pharaonic Egypt, in tempera on plaster: Meidum Geese, Tomb of Nebamun, Tomb of Nefertari, Theban nobles' tombs.

label: Minoan Wall Painting
defn: Fresco painting of Bronze Age Crete and the Minoanised Aegean, c. 1700–1450 BC: Bull-Leaping Fresco from Knossos, Akrotiri Spring Fresco, Fisherman of Thera.
aliases: Minoan frescoes;Aegean wall painting;Wall Paintings of Thera

label: Etruscan Tomb Painting
defn: Painted chamber tombs of Etruria, 7th–2nd century BC, chiefly at Tarquinia and Cerveteri: Tomb of the Leopards, Tomb of the Triclinium, François Tomb at Vulci.

label: Ancient Greek Painting
defn: Surviving Greek wall painting, mostly from tombs of the 5th–3rd century BC in Macedonia, Thrace and Magna Graecia: Tomb of Philip II at Vergina, Thracian Tomb of Kazanlak, Tomb of the Diver at Paestum.

label: Pompeian Wall Painting
defn: Roman wall painting of the Vesuvian cities and Rome, classed by August Mau in four Pompeian Styles, 2nd century BC – AD 79: Villa of the Mysteries, Villa of Poppaea at Oplontis, House of the Vettii.

label: Catacomb Painting
defn: Early Christian and Jewish funerary and devotional wall painting of the 2nd–5th century, above all in the catacombs of Rome and at Dura-Europos: Catacomb of Priscilla, Via Latina catacomb, Dura-Europos synagogue.

label: Byzantine Wall Painting
defn: Fresco programmes of Byzantine and post-Byzantine churches, 6th–15th century: Cappadocian rock-cut churches, painted churches of Troödos, Panselinos at the Protaton, Mystras.

label: Faras Wall Paintings
defn: Wall paintings of the cathedral of Faras in the Nubian kingdom of Makuria, 8th–14th century, removed in 1961–64 to Warsaw and Khartoum: Bishop Petros with St Peter, Saint Anne, Nativity.
attest: wiki:Faras Gallery at the National Museum in Warsaw

label: Hellenistic Mosaics
defn: Greek floor mosaics from the 5th to the 1st century BC, from pebble mosaics to tessellated opus vermiculatum: Pella stag hunt, Alexander Mosaic, Sosos's unswept floor.

label: Roman Mosaics
defn: Floor and wall mosaics of the Roman world, 1st century BC – 5th century AD, with strong regional schools in North Africa, Antioch and Sicily: Nile mosaic of Palestrina, Antioch mosaics, Villa Romana del Casale, Bardo mosaics.

label: Byzantine Mosaics
defn: Glass and stone wall mosaics of Byzantine churches and of the workshops they trained, 5th–14th century: San Vitale, Ravenna, Hagia Sophia, Daphni and Hosios Loukas, Monreale, San Marco.

label: Borgia Group
defn: The pre-Hispanic ritual and divinatory screenfold codices painted on deerskin in the Mixteca-Puebla style of central Mexico, 14th–early 16th century: Codex Borgia, Codex Laud, Codex Fejérváry-Mayer, Codex Cospi.
see: A1-17 Mixtec Codices;A1-18 Aztec Codices;C2-12 Maya Codices

label: Mixtec Codices
defn: Genealogical and historical screenfold codices painted on deerskin by Mixtec (Ñudzavui) tlacuiloque of Oaxaca, 14th–16th century: Codex Zouche-Nuttall, Codex Vindobonensis Mexicanus I, Codex Bodley, Codex Colombino.

label: Aztec Codices
defn: Pictorial manuscripts of the Nahua of central Mexico, from the few pre-Hispanic and early colonial ritual books to the colonial histories, tribute rolls and encyclopedias painted by indigenous tlacuiloque: Codex Borbonicus, Codex Mendoza, Florentine Codex, Codex Azcatitlan.

label: New Spanish Baroque
defn: The painting of the Viceroyalty of New Spain in the Baroque idiom, 17th–18th century, from the large altarpieces and sacristy canvases of Mexico City to devotional and civic pictures: Villalpando's Puebla cathedral dome, Juan Correa's sacristy canvases, Miguel Cabrera's Virgins of Guadalupe.
see: A5-6 Casta Painting;A5-7 Enconchado;A5-8 Biombo;A5-9 Cusco School

label: Casta Painting
defn: Sets of paintings made in 18th-century New Spain (and occasionally Peru) depicting the hierarchy of racial mixtures as family groups with their dress and produce: Miguel Cabrera's casta series (1763), José de Páez series.

label: Enconchado
defn: Paintings of late 17th- and early 18th-century New Spain in oil on panel with inlaid fragments of mother-of-pearl under translucent glazes, influenced by Japanese namban lacquer: González family Conquest of Mexico series, Virgin of Guadalupe (1698).
see: A5-5 New Spanish Baroque;A5-8 Biombo;I2-8 Mexican Lacquerware

label: Biombo
defn: Painted folding screens made in New Spain from the early 17th century after Japanese byōbu, with views of Mexico City, the Conquest and festivities: Biombo of the Conquest and View of Mexico City, Indian wedding and flying pole screen.

label: Cusco School
defn: The school of religious painting centred on Cusco in the Viceroyalty of Peru, 16th–18th century, with Andean painters working from Flemish prints and adding brocade gold (brocateado) and local flora: Corpus Christi series, archangel arquebusiers, Diego Quispe Tito's zodiac series.
see: A5-10 Potosí School;A5-11 Quito School;A5-5 New Spanish Baroque

label: Potosí School
defn: The school of painting of the silver city of Potosí in Upper Peru (Bolivia), 17th–18th century, led by Melchor Pérez de Holguín: Entry of Viceroy Morcillo into Potosí, Virgin of the Cerro.

label: Quito School
defn: The painting and polychrome sculpture of the Audiencia of Quito, 16th–18th century, known for its realist carved and estofado images and its painting workshops: Miguel de Santiago's Augustinian series, Legarda's winged Virgin of Quito, Caspicara's sculptural groups.

label: Retablo
defn: Small devotional paintings of saints in oil on tin (lámina) made by popular painters in Mexico in the 19th century, with the related ex-voto paintings giving thanks for a miracle: Santo Niño de Atocha láminas, ex-votos of San Juan de los Lagos.

label: Amate Painting
defn: Painting in bright colours on amate bark paper by Nahua artists of the Alto Balsas in Guerrero since the 1960s, with Otomí paper cut-figures from San Pablito: village fiesta scenes, birds and flowers.

label: Tablas de Sarhua
defn: Painted boards of Sarhua (Ayacucho), originally genealogical beams given at house-raisings, later sold as narrative paintings of village life: house-beam tablas, Piraq Causa series.

label: Tigua Painting
defn: Painting on stretched sheepskin by Kichwa artists of Tigua in Ecuador's central highlands, begun by Julio Toaquiza in the 1970s, depicting fiestas and Andean landscapes: Corpus Christi dancers, Cotopaxi landscapes.

label: Fileteado
defn: The decorative painting of Buenos Aires carts, buses and shop signs with scrolls, flowers and lettering, inscribed by UNESCO in 2015: colectivo panels, filete signboards.

label: Cordel Literature
defn: The chapbooks of north-eastern Brazil sold hung on strings, whose covers are woodcuts (xilogravura) by popular printmakers: J. Borges woodcuts, cordel covers of Caruaru and Juazeiro.

label: Maya Codices
defn: The surviving bark-paper screenfold books of the Postclassic Maya, written in hieroglyphs with painted almanacs: Dresden Codex, Madrid Codex, Paris Codex, Maya Codex of Mexico.
see: A1-16 Borgia Group;L2-32 Maya Mural Painting

label: Papel Picado
defn: Mexican cut tissue paper banners chiselled through stacked sheets with designs for the Day of the Dead and fiestas.

label: Mesoamerican Jade
defn: Jadeite and greenstone carved by the peoples of Mesoamerica and Costa Rica from the Olmec to the Aztec, as masks, figures, celts, earspools and pendants: Olmec votive axes, Maya jade mosaic masks of Palenque and Calakmul, Costa Rican axe-god pendants.

label: Olmec Sculpture
defn: The stone sculpture of the Olmec of the Gulf Coast, c. 1500–400 BCE, from monumental basalt carving to small greenstone figures and ceramic hollow babies: colossal heads of San Lorenzo and La Venta, La Venta Altar 4, Las Limas Monument 1.
see: D3-6 Mesoamerican Jade;D5-55 Classic Veracruz Sculpture

label: Maya Sculpture
defn: The carved stone and stucco sculpture of the Classic and Postclassic Maya: dated stelae, altars, lintels and panels with rulers and glyphic texts: Copán stelae, Yaxchilan Lintel 24, Piedras Negras Panel 3, Palenque stuccos.
see: E1-36 Maya Ceramics;D3-6 Mesoamerican Jade;L2-32 Maya Mural Painting

label: Aztec Sculpture
defn: The stone sculpture of the Mexica of Tenochtitlan, 14th–16th century, from colossal cult images and calendrical monuments to small household deities: Coatlicue statue, Sun Stone, Stone of Tizoc, Coyolxauhqui Stone.

label: Classic Veracruz Sculpture
defn: The sculpture of the Classic-period Gulf Coast (c. 100–1000 CE): carved stone ballgame yokes, hachas and palmas with scrollwork, and hollow ceramic figures: El Tajín ballcourt panels, Remojadas smiling figures, stone yokes.

label: West Mexican Shaft-Tomb Figures
defn: Hollow and solid ceramic figures and village tableaux placed in shaft tombs of Jalisco, Nayarit and Colima, c. 300 BCE–400 CE: Colima dogs, Nayarit house and ballgame models, Jalisco Ameca figures.

label: Chavín Sculpture
defn: The carved granite of Chavín de Huántar and the Chavín horizon, c. 900–200 BCE, with fanged composite deities in contour-rivalry: Lanzón, Raimondi Stele, Tello Obelisk, tenon heads.

label: Valdivia Figurines
defn: Small fired-clay female figures of the Valdivia culture of coastal Ecuador (c. 3500–1500 BCE), among the earliest ceramics of the Americas: Venus of Valdivia.

label: Estofado
defn: Polychrome wooden sculpture of Spain and Spanish America in which gilded surfaces are painted and scratched to imitate brocade, the technique of viceregal image-makers (imagineros) of Mexico, Guatemala and Quito: Antigua Guatemala saints, Quito sculptural groups.
see: A5-11 Quito School;D5-60 Brazilian Baroque;D5-61 Santos

label: Brazilian Baroque
defn: The sculpture and church decoration of colonial Brazil, 17th–early 19th century, culminating in the Rococo of Minas Gerais: Aleijadinho's soapstone prophets at Congonhas, Mestre Ataíde's ceilings, Bahia gilded talha.

label: Santos
defn: Carved and painted devotional images of saints made by santeros in the Hispanic Caribbean and New Mexico: bultos in the round and painted retablo panels: New Mexican bultos, Puerto Rican santos de palo, Three Kings figures.
see: A6-10 Retablo;D5-59 Estofado;southeast_asia D5-58 Philippine Santos

label: Alebrije
defn: Brightly painted fantastic creatures, first made in papier-mâché by Pedro Linares in Mexico City and from the 1980s carved in copal wood by Zapotec carvers of Oaxaca: Arrazola carvings, San Martín Tilcajete tonas.

label: Cartonería
defn: Mexican papier-mâché sculpture for festivals: Judas figures burned on Holy Saturday, skeletons for the Day of the Dead and mojigangas: Judas figures, Linares calaveras.

label: Caruaru Clay Figures
defn: Small painted clay figures of north-eastern rural life made at Alto do Moura, Caruaru (Pernambuco), after Mestre Vitalino: bands of zabumba players, retirantes, cangaceiros.

label: Haitian Metal Art
defn: Sculpture cut and hammered from flattened oil drums by the smiths of Croix-des-Bouquets after Georges Liautaud: vodou lwa figures, trees of life, mermaids.

label: Taíno Zemís
defn: Sculptural objects of the Taíno of the Greater Antilles that housed deities and ancestral spirits, in stone, wood, shell and cotton, with the ritual seats and cohoba stands of the same cult: three-pointer stones, Vere zemís of Jamaica, duhos.

label: Peruvian Retablo
defn: Portable box altars of Ayacucho (Huamanga) filled with painted plaster and potato-paste figures, from the cajón de San Marcos to scenes of village life: cajón de San Marcos, Joaquín López Antay retablos.

label: Maya Ceramics
defn: The painted and carved pottery of the Classic Maya, above all the polychrome and codex-style cylinder vases and plates with courtly and mythological scenes and glyphic texts: codex-style vases of the Mirador Basin, Ik'-style vases of Motul de San José, Jaina figurines.

label: Teotihuacan Ceramics
defn: The pottery of Teotihuacan (c. 100–650 CE): cylindrical tripod vessels with painted stucco, Thin Orange ware and composite theatre-type censers: stuccoed tripod vases, Thin Orange effigy vessels, theatre censers.

label: Gran Coclé Pottery
defn: The polychrome pottery of central Panama (c. 200–1500 CE) in its named styles, painted with stylised crocodiles, birds and rays: Conté style plates from Sitio Conte, Macaracas pedestal dishes, Parita style.

label: Nicoya Polychrome
defn: The white-slipped polychrome pottery of Greater Nicoya (north-western Costa Rica and Nicaragua), c. 800–1500 CE, with Mexican-derived feathered-serpent motifs: Papagayo polychrome vessels, effigy jars.

label: Moche Ceramics
defn: Mould-made and painted stirrup-spout vessels of the Moche of Peru's north coast (c. 100–800 CE): naturalistic portrait heads, effigy vessels and fineline painted narrative scenes: portrait vessels, Presentation Theme fineline vessels.
see: G1-22 Moche Metalwork;L2-35 Moche Murals;E1-41 Nazca Pottery

label: Nazca Pottery
defn: Slip-painted polychrome pottery of the Nazca of Peru's south coast (c. 100 BCE–700 CE) in up to twelve colours, with mythical beings and trophy heads: double-spout and bridge bottles, Anthropomorphic Mythical Being bowls.

label: Chimú Blackware
defn: The burnished reduction-fired black pottery of the Chimú kingdom of Peru's north coast (c. 900–1470 CE), mould-made in stirrup-spout and effigy forms: stirrup-spout bottles with monkey adornos, double-chambered whistling vessels.

label: Shipibo-Conibo Pottery
defn: Pottery painted by Shipibo-Conibo women of the Peruvian Amazon with the maze-like kené designs that also cover their textiles and bodies: chomo jars, quenti cooking pots.

label: Talavera Poblana
defn: Tin-glazed earthenware of Puebla and Tlaxcala made since the 16th century by guild potters after Spanish maiolica, in blue-and-white and polychrome: tibores, lebrillos, azulejos of Puebla façades.

label: Barro Negro Pottery
defn: Black burnished pottery of San Bartolo Coyotepec (Oaxaca), reduction-fired and polished to a metallic sheen since Doña Rosa in the 1950s: cántaros, openwork vessels.

label: Tonalá Pottery
defn: The burnished and painted pottery of Tonalá and Tlaquepaque in Jalisco, in its colonial and modern styles: bruñido, petatillo, bandera, canelo.

label: Mata Ortiz Pottery
defn: Fine-walled painted pottery of Juan Mata Ortiz (Chihuahua) revived by Juan Quezada from the 1970s after Casas Grandes (Paquimé) wares.

label: Tree of Life
defn: Multi-branched painted clay candelabra-sculptures of Metepec and Izúcar de Matamoros depicting Eden and other narratives: Adam and Eve trees, Soteno family trees.

label: Pucará Bulls
defn: Paired glazed clay bulls of Pucará and Santiago de Pupuja (Puno) set on house roofs for protection and fertility.
see: E1-48 Tree of Life;D5-64 Caruaru Clay Figures

label: Chulucanas Pottery
defn: Burnished and smoke-resist decorated pottery of Chulucanas (Piura), revived from Vicús and Tallán techniques, with a denomination of origin.

label: Quinchamalí Pottery
defn: Black burnished pottery with white incised inlay made by women potters of Quinchamalí and Santa Cruz de Cuca in central Chile (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2022): guitarrera figure, chanchito alcancía.
aliases: Quinchamalí and Santa Cruz de Cuca pottery

label: Awajún Pottery
defn: Pottery made by Awajún women of the Peruvian Amazon with its knowledge and ritual, inscribed by UNESCO in 2021.

label: Goiabeiras Clay Pots
defn: Black clay cooking pots (panelas) of the paneleiras of Goiabeiras in Vitória (Espírito Santo), smoke-blackened with tannin, the first Brazilian intangible heritage registered by IPHAN (2002).
aliases: panelas de barro de Goiabeiras;craft of the clay pot makers of Goiabeiras

label: Moche Metalwork
defn: Gold, silver and gilded-copper objects of the Moche, worked by depletion gilding and inlaid with turquoise and shell: Sipán ear ornaments, backflaps, nose ornaments.

label: Sicán Metalwork
defn: Gold and tumbaga objects of the Sicán (Lambayeque) culture of Peru's north coast (c. 900–1100 CE): Sicán funerary masks, tumi knives, beakers.

label: Chimú Metalwork
defn: Hammered and repoussé silver and gold of the Chimú kingdom (c. 900–1470 CE): beakers, ear spools, feathered tunics with plaques.
see: E1-42 Chimú Blackware;G1-23 Sicán Metalwork;G1-25 Inca Metalwork

label: Inca Metalwork
defn: Gold and silver of the Inca empire (c. 1400–1532): cast and hammered figurines from capacocha offerings, keros and ornaments: silver llamas, gold female figurines.

label: Muisca Goldwork
defn: Lost-wax tumbaga castings of the Muisca of the Colombian highlands (c. 600–1600 CE), above all the votive tunjos: Muisca raft, tunjo figures.

label: Colonial Andean Silverwork
defn: The silver of the Viceroyalty of Peru (16th–19th century) from Potosí, Cusco and Lima: church plate, sahumadores, and the domestic and equestrian silver that continued in the Río de la Plata: incense burners in animal form, mate cups, altar frontals.
see: G3-12 Mapuche Silverwork;H2-6 Colonial Andean Tapestry

label: Tairona Goldwork
defn: Cast gold and tumbaga ornaments of the Tairona of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (c. 900–1600 CE): bat-man and eagle pendants, nose ornaments, labrets.

label: Quimbaya Goldwork
defn: The gold of the Quimbaya of the Middle Cauca valley, with its ceramics: Quimbaya Treasure poporos, seated figures, helmets.

label: Calima Goldwork
defn: Hammered and cast gold of the Calima region of south-western Colombia in its Ilama, Yotoco and Malagana phases: diadems, nose rings, pectorals with faces.

label: Tolima Goldwork
defn: Flat cast gold pendants of the Tolima region of the Magdalena valley, with anchor-shaped human-bat figures.

label: Isthmian Goldwork
defn: Cast and hammered gold and tumbaga ornaments of the chiefdoms of Panama and Costa Rica (c. 200–1500 CE) in the Coclé, Veraguas, Chiriquí and Diquís styles: Sitio Conte plaques, eagle pendants, crocodile deity figures.
see: E1-38 Gran Coclé Pottery;G3-6 Tairona Goldwork

label: Mixtec Goldwork
defn: Lost-wax cast gold ornaments of the Postclassic Mixtec of Oaxaca, with filigree-effect wax threads: Monte Albán Tomb 7 pectorals, labrets, bell pendants.

label: Mapuche Silverwork
defn: The silver jewellery of Mapuche women in Chile and Argentina, flourishing from the 18th century: trapelacucha pectorals, tupu pins, trarilonco headbands.

label: Inca Textiles
defn: The tapestry-woven cumbi cloth of the Inca state, woven by aqllakuna and cumbicamayoc, with tocapu tunics as the highest rank: Dumbarton Oaks tocapu tunic, checkerboard military tunics.
see: H2-5 Wari Textiles;H2-6 Colonial Andean Tapestry;H2-7 Andean Textiles

label: Wari Textiles
defn: The interlocking tapestry tunics of the Wari state (c. 600–1000 CE) with abstracted staff-god profiles expanded and compressed across the field.

label: Colonial Andean Tapestry
defn: Tapestry-woven textiles of the Viceroyalty of Peru (16th–19th century) in which cumbi weavers combined Inca, Spanish and Asian designs: colonial uncus with tocapu, tapices with coats of arms.
see: H2-4 Inca Textiles;G1-27 Colonial Andean Silverwork

label: Andean Textiles
defn: The living warp-faced and complementary-warp weaving of Quechua and Aymara communities of Peru, Bolivia and Ecuador, with named regional styles: Jalq'a and Tarabuco axsus, Chinchero lliclla, Otavalo weaving.
see: H2-8 Taquile Textile Art;H2-4 Inca Textiles

label: Taquile Textile Art
defn: The weaving and knitting of Taquile Island in Lake Titicaca, where men knit chullos and women weave belts (chumpi) recording the agricultural calendar, inscribed by UNESCO in 2008.

label: Saltillo Serape
defn: Tapestry-woven wool blankets of Saltillo and northern Mexico (18th–19th century) with a central diamond medallion and serrated fields.

label: Maya Textiles
defn: The backstrap-woven and brocaded cotton cloth of the Maya of Guatemala and Chiapas, whose huipiles, sashes and headcloths are distinct by town and community: Chichicastenango huipiles, Santiago Atitlán tzutes, Chamula wool.

label: Chancay Textiles
defn: Cotton and camelid cloth of the Chancay culture of Peru's central coast (c. 1000–1470 CE): gauze and openwork, painted cloth and woven dolls: gauze panels, painted cloths.

label: Paracas Textiles
defn: Camelid-wool embroidered mantles from the Paracas Necropolis on Peru's south coast (c. 300 BCE–200 CE), stem-stitched with repeating flying figures: Paracas Necropolis mantles.

label: Mola
defn: Reverse-appliqué cotton panels made by Guna women of Panama and Colombia for the front and back of their blouses.

label: Arpillera
defn: Appliqué and embroidered burlap-backed pictures made by women's workshops in Chile under the Pinochet dictatorship and later in Peru.

label: Drapo Vodou
defn: Sequinned and beaded ritual flags of Haitian Vodou, carried to salute the lwa: vèvè flags, Myrlande Constant tapestries.

label: Ñandutí
defn: Paraguayan needle lace of radiating spider-web suns, made in Itauguá.

label: Divina Pastora Irish Lace
defn: The needle lace (renda irlandesa) made with cord and buttonhole stitches in Divina Pastora, Sergipe, registered by IPHAN.

label: Rebozo
defn: The Mexican woman's shawl, at its finest in warp-ikat (jaspe) cotton and silk with knotted fringe from Santa María del Río and Tenancingo.

label: Panama Hat
defn: Hats plaited from toquilla palm straw in Ecuador (Montecristi, Cuenca), inscribed by UNESCO in 2012.

label: Mexican Featherwork
defn: Feather mosaic of Mesoamerica and colonial New Spain (amanteca), from Aztec shields and headdresses to Christian feather paintings: Moctezuma's headdress, Mass of Saint Gregory (1539).

label: Mate Burilado
defn: Engraved and pyrographed gourds of the central Peruvian Andes (Huanta, Cochas Chico), with dense narrative scenes.

label: Mexican Lacquerware
defn: Lacquer (maque) of Mexico made with insect and seed-oil lacquers on gourds and wood, by inlay or painting, in its regional centres: Olinalá boxes, Pátzcuaro gilded trays, Chiapa de Corzo gourds.

label: Barniz de Pasto
defn: Decoration of wood with sheets of mopa-mopa resin cut and applied in colour, practised in Pasto (Nariño) since the colonial period (UNESCO urgent safeguarding 2020).

label: Cueva de las Manos
defn: Stencilled hands and hunting scenes of guanacos painted in the Río Pinturas caves of Patagonia from c. 9300 BP (UNESCO 1999).
see: L1-13 Serra da Capivara Rock Art

label: Serra da Capivara Rock Art
defn: The painted rock shelters of Serra da Capivara (Piauí), with Nordeste-tradition hunting, dancing and sexual scenes (UNESCO 1991): Pedra Furada, Toca do Boqueirão.
see: L1-12 Cueva de las Manos;L1-15 Chiribiquete Rock Paintings

label: Toro Muerto Petroglyphs
defn: Thousands of petroglyphs pecked on volcanic boulders at Toro Muerto (Arequipa) with dancers, camelids and birds, with related Andean sites: Toro Muerto, Toquepala Caves, Miculla.

label: Chiribiquete Rock Paintings
defn: Red-ochre paintings of jaguars, hunters and dancers on the tepuis of Chiribiquete in the Colombian Amazon (UNESCO 2018).
see: L1-13 Serra da Capivara Rock Art

label: Maya Mural Painting
defn: The wall paintings of the Maya from the Preclassic to the Postclassic: San Bartolo murals, Bonampak Room 2 battle, Calakmul market murals.

label: Teotihuacan Mural Painting
defn: The fresco painting of the apartment compounds of Teotihuacan (c. 200–650 CE): Tepantitla Great Goddess, Tetitla, Atetelco.

label: Cacaxtla Murals
defn: The Epiclassic murals of Cacaxtla (Tlaxcala, c. 650–900 CE), mixing Maya and central Mexican styles: Battle Mural, Bird Man.
see: L2-32 Maya Mural Painting;L2-33 Teotihuacan Mural Painting

label: Moche Murals
defn: Painted and modelled mud-plaster friezes of Moche temples: Huaca de la Luna Ai Apaec friezes, El Brujo.

label: Mexican Muralism
defn: The public mural movement of post-revolutionary Mexico (1920s–1970s) led by Rivera, Orozco and Siqueiros: Rivera's National Palace murals, Orozco's Hospicio Cabañas, Siqueiros' Polyforum.
see: L2-37 Chilean Muralism;L2-38 Murals of Revolutionary Nicaragua

label: Chilean Muralism
defn: Chilean public mural painting from the 1940s, from Siqueiros' Chillán murals to the brigade painting of the Brigada Ramona Parra.

label: Murals of Revolutionary Nicaragua
defn: Public murals painted in Sandinista Nicaragua (1979–1990) by Nicaraguan and international brigades.

label: Nazca Lines
defn: Geoglyphs scraped into the desert of the Nazca and Palpa pampas (c. 500 BCE–500 CE), with straight lines and animal figures (UNESCO 1994): Hummingbird, Monkey, Condor, Palpa figures.

label: Pintados Geoglyphs
defn: Hillside geoglyphs of the Atacama made by removing or piling stones (c. 600–1500 CE): Cerro Pintados panels, Atacama Giant, Chug-Chug.

label: Acre Geoglyphs
defn: Geometric ditched enclosures of the south-western Amazon (Acre, Brazil), c. 0–1300 CE.
